update.title: Built a shared history database for system activity
update.summary: Built a PostgreSQL history store for tool operations and artifacts, with a normalized SQLAlchemy schema, repository API, and provenance queries.
update.previewAlt: The first recorded Constellation History Database output and its linked artifacts

blocks.body:
## Give tool activity a shared data model

I built a shared history database for Constellation Framework so local tools can record operations and the files they consume or produce without inventing a separate log format for every integration. PostgreSQL provides transactions, relational constraints, time-aware queries, and JSONB fields for tool-specific configuration.

The schema separates operations, artifacts, and tags. An operation stores its type, owning tool, optional model, start and completion times, duration, status, error, configuration, and an optional parent operation. Artifacts store a stable UUID, resolved path, file type, size, checksum, MIME type, timestamp, and flexible metadata. Junction tables link inputs, outputs, and tags without copying file records into every event.

## Preserve lineage, not just a list of events

The repository supports both long-running and one-shot work. A caller can start an operation, register inputs as they become known, attach outputs, and complete with success or failure. A convenience path performs the same lifecycle for work that has already completed. Artifact registration is idempotent by resolved path and computes SHA-256 for files below the configured 100 MB threshold.

Queries cover recent operations, time ranges, tools, operation types, tags, artifact history, and parent-operation chains. The first database run records two successful operations at 19:43 on November 16. Its ComfyUI image-generation record links `test_prompt.txt` as an input and `test_output.png` as an output, exercising operation-to-artifact lineage end to end.

## Keep the boundary practical

SQLAlchemy supplies the model and repository boundary. Alembic is configured to generate, apply, and roll back schema migrations. Local connections use peer authentication over a PostgreSQL Unix socket, while direct SQL examples and `pg_dump`/restore procedures keep the store inspectable outside the Python API.

The schema models operations and artifacts independently, then uses explicit relations for inputs, outputs, tags, and operation chains.
blocks.code:
erDiagram
  OPERATION ||--o{ OPERATION_INPUT : consumes
  ARTIFACT ||--o{ OPERATION_INPUT : is_input
  OPERATION ||--o{ OPERATION_OUTPUT : produces
  ARTIFACT ||--o{ OPERATION_OUTPUT : is_output
  OPERATION }o--o{ TAG : categorized_by
  OPERATION o|--o{ OPERATION : parent_of

  OPERATION {
    uuid id
    string operation_type
    string tool_name
    string status
    timestamp started_at
    timestamp completed_at
    jsonb config
  }
  ARTIFACT {
    uuid id
    text file_path
    string file_type
    string checksum
    jsonb metadata
  }
